title: IUPAC Classification and Periodic Trends
topicTitle: IUPAC classification of elements; periodic trend and periodicity: atomic radii, ionic radii, ionization energy, electron affinity, electronegativity, metallic characters
notes: **IUPAC numbering:** groups are numbered 1 to 18 from left to right. This replaced the older Roman numeral system.
**Atomic radius trend:** decreases across a period (increasing $Z_{eff}$ pulls electrons closer) and increases down a group (additional shells).
**Ionic radius:** cations are smaller than parent atoms (loss of electrons reduces electron-electron repulsion); anions are larger (gain of electrons increases repulsion).
**Ionization energy:** energy to remove an electron. Increases across a period, decreases down a group. Noble gases have the highest IE because of stable filled shells.
**Electron affinity:** energy change when an electron is added. Becomes more negative across a period (except noble gases) and less negative down a group.
**Electronegativity:** ability to attract bonding electrons. Increases across a period and decreases down a group. Fluorine is the most electronegative element (3.98 on Pauling scale).
**Metallic character:** decreases across a period and increases down a group. Metals are on the left and centre; non-metals on the upper right.
